Eligibility.metaTitle: Can I take traffic school? Eligibility check
Eligibility.metaDescription: Answer 5 yes/no questions to see whether California traffic school is likely an option for your ticket.
Eligibility.title: Can I take traffic school?
Eligibility.intro: Answer 5 quick questions. Nothing you enter is saved.
Eligibility.disclaimer: This is general guidance for a demo. Your court always makes the final decision.

questions.validLicense: Do you have a valid driver's license?
questions.courtAllowed: Has the court allowed you to attend traffic school for this ticket?
questions.noRecentSchool: Have you gone at least 18 months without attending traffic school?
questions.nonCommercial: Were you driving a non-commercial vehicle with a non-commercial license?
questions.eligibleViolation: Is your ticket for a minor moving violation (for example speeding or a missed stop sign)?

Eligibility.eligibleText: Based on your answers, traffic school looks like an option. Confirm with your court, then choose your course language.
Eligibility.notEligibleTitle: Traffic school is probably not an option

nextStep.validLicense: Traffic school needs a valid driver's license. Contact your court about other options.
nextStep.courtAllowed: Only the court can allow traffic school. Ask your court, or check the notice it sent you.
nextStep.noRecentSchool: You can usually attend traffic school only once in 18 months. Your court can tell you what to do instead.
nextStep.nonCommercial: Commercial drivers and vehicles usually can't use traffic school to mask a ticket. Ask your court about your options.
nextStep.eligibleViolation: Some violations don't qualify. Your court decides, so ask it whether yours does.

0.q: Do you have a valid driver's license?
0.a: Traffic school is offered to licensed drivers. If your license is suspended or expired, the court will usually want that sorted out first.

1.q: Has the court allowed you to attend traffic school for this ticket?
1.a: Only the court can approve traffic school. Look for a line on your notice or on the court's website, or ask the clerk.

2.q: Is your ticket for a minor moving violation (for example speeding or a missed stop sign)?
2.a: Most basic moving violations qualify. Parking, equipment and registration tickets usually do not.

3.q: Have you gone at least 18 months without attending traffic school?
3.a: You can normally use traffic school once every 18 months, counted from the date of your last violation that used it.

4.q: Were you driving a non-commercial vehicle with a non-commercial license?
4.a: The rule looks at both the vehicle you drove and the license you hold. The next section explains the difference.

Eligibility.noHeading: Why a court may say no

noItems.0: A violation committed in a commercial vehicle
noItems.3: Reckless driving or a violation worth more than one point
noItems.4: Failing to stop after an accident
noItems.7: A ticket with an unresolved failure-to-appear

Eligibility.vehicleHeading: The vehicle and the license are two different rules

0.t: You were driving a commercial vehicle
0.b: Tickets earned in a commercial vehicle are not eligible, even if you hold a regular license.

1.t: You hold a commercial license but drove your own car
1.b: This one depends on the court. Ask before you pay for a course.

Eligibility.pointHeading: Traffic school hides the point. It does not delete the ticket.
Eligibility.pointBody: You still pay the fine and the court fee. After you finish, the court keeps the violation point from showing on your driving record for insurance purposes.

0.q: Does this tool give legal advice?
0.a: No. It is general guidance for a demo project. Your court always makes the final decision.

1.a: No. Your answers stay in your browser.

2.q: How long do I have to finish the course?
2.a: Your court sets the deadline. It is printed on your notice.
